### Architect · Answer

Event: `484947daa09babab5848c0905e5a4c09` · 2026-09-30T06:01:03Z

> K9 design: settled from the pages; no owner choice. Targets are the owner's (pre-ruled); the rest is R10/I1/I2/R6 + tenet 1.
> 
> Direction: a destruction walks what the dying subtree holds and what names it, never every object frame. Three changes:
> 
> 1. Child links. Add first_child/next_sibling to the budget frame; mark_dying, lift_dying and destroy_marked's free loop walk the subtree instead of 0..=high_frame.
> 2. Owner lists. Each budget heads the endpoints/devices charged to it; message::budgets_dying ends exactly the subtree's. Process objects need no change (PID index, 64 lookups).
> 3. One sweep. Fold free_object/destroy_endpoint/destroy_device's sweeps into destroy_marked's single pass; defer the frame frees past it (I1). The one pass walks live handle-table pages, bounded by MAX_PROCESS_COUNT×MAX_HANDLE_PAGES; a budget filling the system with endpoints cannot grow it (a process past MAX_HANDLES creates none).
> 
> Invariant: R10's own — no handle/queued message/taken call keeps authority via a dying budget (I2), no handle names a freed frame (I1), ledger returns exactly (I10). check_all_dying/check_process_index/check_irq_index re-scans stay as the audit and must not move onto the destruction walk (sched-latency measures the checked build).
> 
> Design on docs/kernel/budgets.md residual risks. Brief at .wash/local/K9-implementer.md (reading list, owned paths, traps: checked-build scans, R10 step order, every link has two ends, free_object's two paths, GATE1's full fill restored, rv32 frame words).
> 
> Escape hatch (arch, not owner, unneeded for 30/40 ms): a full handle reverse index needs per-handle pointers and changes the 128-slots cost model. The bounded sweep should fit with margin; reopen here rather than widen if not.
